Design decision from Jack Heart (2026-11-22) on data ownership, storage/DB, and latency (Fork #1):

"Ok lets start with 1: - the key claim is \"You own your own data\". It is totally ok for us to also have a a different version of itin  a DB for speed. Subsecond graph loads is a compelte requirement. in terms of how data flows, whatever is fastest and most reliable"

Key implications:
- "You own your own data" (files in the user's directory/bucket remain the portable, user-owned record) does NOT forbid maintaining a derived/indexed copy in a database for speed.
- Sub-second graph loads is a hard requirement (cannot put multi-second/hundred-second full rebuilds in front of chart loads).
- Choose the fastest, most reliable live data flow (e.g. live ingestion/indexing into a DB alongside durable run files) rather than restricting the view to slow on-demand file/bucket scans.
